heading: Types
text:
### Types [IRET.3.1]

A slot value is a **tagged union** — a kind discriminant plus exactly one
payload. Its storage differs by kind in a way that matters:

| Kind | Payload | Storage |
|---|---|---|
| Int | 64-bit signed | inline |
| Float | double | inline |
| Bool | boolean | inline |
| Time | UTC nanoseconds and a zone offset | inline |
| Null | none | inline |
| String, Bytes | pointer **and length** | **interned**, not owned by the value |
| FactRef | the target's fact id, never a pointer | inline |
| Json | UTF-8 document tree | **heap-allocated**, owned; or borrowed from the wrapper that owns it |
| Unbound, Ratio | none; numerator and denominator | inline; evaluator-only ([IRET.1.3]) |

Three kinds reach outside the value. A String or Bytes is a borrowed
view into the intern table, so copying a value never copies string bytes
and comparing two interned strings can be a pointer comparison. Json is
the one kind that owns heap memory, which is why it is the kind the
bounded-memory dialects restrict ([LNLS.3.1]). A FactRef holds an id, so
a target that leaves working memory leaves no dangling pointer.

The explicit length on String and Bytes means a value is not
NUL-terminated by contract; a reader must use the length rather than
scanning.
